task: MM-FIX-2 — Define Maven cross-module duplicate TestIdentity ownership policy
mainStpAfter: SELF (the focused commit containing this verification artifact)

duplicateClassification.evidence: The checked-in sources differ only by wildcard versus explicit imports. javap -v shows identical executable instructions and annotations; class bytes differ in LineNumberTable entries because the explicit imports add ten lines. Raw source and class hashes are therefore intentionally unequal.

rootCause: SonarJava contains two separately compiled checked-in copies of ReassignmentFinderTest: one in java-checks-common and one in java-checks. java-checks also has a normal Maven dependency on java-checks-common, but the collision comes from both modules' own target/test-classes roots, not from transitive classpath scanning. Ordinary Surefire executes both copies.
ownershipSelectionRule: A logical identity has safe Maven inventory ownership only when it is discovered from exactly one module test-output root. Reuse visible only on dependency classpaths does not create another owner. Any identity discovered from two or more module test-output roots remains fatal, regardless of byte equivalence, because the existing mapping pipeline can execute and publish each root independently.

mappingSafetyAnalysis.assignmentRouting: A shard assignment contains only className#method and has no module coordinate. Both owning modules rediscover and accept it.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.surefireIncludes: The same logical include can match both module-local test classes.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.moduleLocalExecution: SonarJava ordinary reports prove two executions per duplicate identity.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.moduleLocalFragmentProduction: Both modules can produce a coverage/evidence entry with the same identity.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.reactorAggregation: AggregateReactorCoverageFragmentMojo rejects duplicate fragment and evidence owners.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.coverageUnion: Not safe: union would erase provenance and can combine coverage from two physical executions.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.executionEvidence: Not safe to collapse: two physical executions cannot be represented as one unambiguous owner.
mappingSafetyAnalysis.decision: Duplicate mapping must fail; no mapping changes were made.

implementation.behavior: Collect every occurrence before validation and report every unsafe group deterministically with Maven coordinates, class/source paths, and SHA-256 hashes.
